Following up on the [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150734#issuecomment-5711038730): the introduced hardlink regression is fixed in `c0b3a9d2f00`.

Workspace saves request hardlink rejection; the node checks both preflight and the actual opened write handle. The existing preflight acknowledges support, so an older node that ignores the option cannot proceed to the mutating call. Ordinary `file.write` preserves its existing behavior.

All 78 focused tests pass on this PR, including the real-handler workspace test asserting both the Agent document and its outside hardlink remain unchanged after refusal. This is local handler/adapter proof, not an Enterprise deployment claim.

The separate in-flight revocation/replacement concern remains an accepted timing limitation, documented in #150584 and [OCE #76](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/issues/76). We are not claiming cancellation or rollback of a previously dispatched write.

The service-owned contract is intentional: document/bootstrap access must work outside an active harness turn. The service may invoke only its owning plugin's registered commands, and those calls still pass node file policy and service-lifetime checks. Incoming API handlers keep their own caller authorization. This is the bounded contract proposed by this PR, not a general service shell capability.

The documented non-rollback limit is accepted: retiring access blocks new dispatch and stale results but does not undo a write already dispatched. Mapped workspaces require compatible node commands; incompatible or disconnected nodes fail explicitly rather than selecting a local copy. Unconfigured workspaces keep the existing local path.

Current head `7121eaea9c92` includes the fixed foundation and the hardlink refusal checks. No persistent document schema or database migration is introduced here. These design decisions do not assert separate security-owner sign-off; the SDK expansion has maintainer approval, and CI is still running.
